program_note:
Four Rubáiyát is a setting of four of the quatrains from the second edition of Edward Fitzgerald’s Rubaiyat of Omar Khayyam.  Fitzgerald’s landmark 19th-century work is in part a translation and in part a “transmogrification” of portions of the collection of Khayyám’s original 11th to 12th-century poems.  Whether read in the original, in translation, or in the transmogrifications, underlying all of the poems is a rebuff of false piety in favor of a more honest appreciation of a virtuous life.  While not endorsing hedonism, Khayyám clearly believed that a virtuous life is not one without sensual pleasures.

The four quatrains in this setting are grouped into three movements.  The first, “Why, be this Juice the growth of God” (LXIII in the 2nd Edition), celebrates the joy of life; the second, “Waste not your Hour/The Moving Finger” (LVI & LXXVI) cautions us of the limited time we have on earth; and the last, “Ah, with the Grape” (XCVIII) is a glance towards the grave.

The total duration of the three movements is approximately 6:00, divided into 1:00, 2:40, and 2:20, respectively.

Four Rubáiyát was written for and commissioned by Scott Tucker and the Cornell University Glee Club.

David S. Lefkowitz

Los Angeles, CA

29 June, 2010
